canonical_statement: The review aimed to evaluate the comparative safety and efficacy of sedative drugs used for tracheal intubation of critically ill patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We aim to perform a systematic review and network meta-analysis to evaluate the safety and efficacy of different sedative drugs for tracheal intubation of critically ill patients.

canonical_statement: The review followed PRISMA-NMA reporting guidance and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO as CRD42024600739 on October 25, 2024.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Network Meta-analysis Extension (PRISMA-NMA) statement... We prospectively registered the protocol... (CRD42024600739).

canonical_statement: Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials enrolling adults or children older than 28 days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We included all RCTs whether using parallel or cluster-based randomization... enrolled adults or children > 28 days of age.

population.label: Adults or children older than 28 days

canonical_statement: Eligible studies examined tracheal intubation of critically ill patients in the emergency department, ICU, operating room, or out-of-hospital setting, with operating-room studies restricted to critical illness, emergency surgery for a critical condition, or acute physiologic compromise.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: examined intubation in critically ill patients in the emergency department (ED), ICU, operating room (OR), or out of hospital setting...

population.label: Critically ill patients requiring tracheal intubation
inclusion_criteria: ED, ICU, OR, or out-of-hospital intubation
OR studies required critical illness/emergency critical condition/acute physiologic compromise

canonical_statement: Eligible trials compared sedative induction strategies including propofol, ketamine, ketamine-propofol, etomidate, midazolam, thiopental, methohexital, or opioid-containing sedative nodes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: compared any combination of sedative drugs including, but not limited to: propofol and ketamine, both separately and in combination; etomidate; midazolam; thiopental; and methohexital...

population.label: Critically ill patients in eligible sedative-comparison RCTs

canonical_statement: The search covered MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, the Cochrane Library, the Cochrane trial registry, selected conference abstracts, and trial registries from inception through December 10, 2025 without language restriction.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We searched the following electronic databases: MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, the Cochrane Library, and the Cochrane trial registry... with no language restriction and from inception to December 10, 2025.

canonical_statement: Title/abstract screening and full-text review were performed independently and in duplicate, with disagreements resolved by discussion and consensus.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Screening of titles and abstracts was performed independently and in duplicate... Full texts were then reviewed, again independently and in duplicate... Disagreements... were resolved through discussion and consensus.

canonical_statement: Data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment were performed independently and in duplicate; risk of bias was assessed with a modified Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we extracted the following data independently and in duplicate... assessed risk of bias... independently and in duplicate using the modified Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool.

canonical_statement: Conventional meta-analyses used DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models, risk ratios for dichotomous outcomes, mean differences for continuous outcomes, and 95% confidence intervals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we used the DerSimonian and Laird random-effects model... For dichotomous outcomes we calculated the relative risk (RR)... For continuous outcomes we calculated the mean difference (MD)...

canonical_statement: Network meta-analysis used a contrast-based random-effects model with a common heterogeneity estimate and multivariate meta-analysis in Stata 18.5, with transitivity and incoherence assessments when network structure permitted.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For NMA, we used a contrast-based random-effects model with a common heterogeneity estimate and multivariate meta-analysis using the network suite in Stata...

canonical_statement: The certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE for direct, indirect, and network estimates with a minimally contextualized framework.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We used the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach to assess the certainty of evidence for each outcome.

canonical_statement: The prespecified sensitivity analyses included exclusion of pediatric patients; a post-hoc sensitivity analysis excluded opioid-containing nodes, and a post-hoc pairwise analysis evaluated 28/30-day mortality for etomidate versus ketamine.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We planned for a priori sensitivity analysis excluding pediatric patients and performed a post-hoc sensitivity analysis excluding any nodes with opioids. Conventional pairwise meta-analysis was conducted as a post-hoc sensitivity analysis...

canonical_statement: Hemodynamic instability during intubation was defined by individual study authors and most commonly used post-induction systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg, with other definitions including lower pressure thresholds, absolute/relative blood-pressure decreases, and/or new or increased vasopressor use.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Most commonly, studies used a post-induction systolic blood pressure (SBP) < 90 mmHg... Other accepted definitions included an absolute or relative SBP decrease... and/or new or increased vasopressor requirement.

outcome.definition: Study-specific; most commonly post-induction SBP <90 mmHg, with alternative thresholds/decreases and/or vasopressor criteria.

canonical_statement: Mortality was pooled at the longest reported time point for each trial when multiple mortality time points were available.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For the mortality analysis we pooled mortality at the longest time point reported by each trial; where a trial reported mortality at multiple time points, the longest available time point was used.

concept.text: mortality at longest reported time point

outcome.definition: Longest available mortality time point from each trial.

canonical_statement: Initiation of post-intubation continuous infusion vasopressors was treated as a distinct outcome from immediate hemodynamic instability during intubation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We retained these as separate outcomes, rather than combining them, because they were reported separately by most of the eligible trials, occur over different time horizons, and may carry different clinical implications.

concept.text: initiation of post-intubation continuous infusion vasopressors

outcome.definition: Clinical decision to initiate ongoing vasoactive support after intubation; kept separate from immediate peri-intubation hemodynamic instability.

canonical_statement: Adrenal suppression was defined variably across studies and was analyzed as biochemical adrenal suppression.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Seven studies reported on biochemical adrenal suppression. Adrenal suppression was defined variably across studies.

outcome.definition: Study-specific biochemical adrenal suppression definition.

canonical_statement: The review included 21 randomized controlled trials with 6,031 participants.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: included 21 RCTs with a total of 6,031 patients in the analysis

population.label: Participants in 21 included RCTs

canonical_statement: The mean age across included studies was 58 ± 8.2 years, and the included trials spanned ED, ICU, operating-room, out-of-hospital, mixed, and unspecified settings.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The mean age of enrolled patients across studies was 58 ± 8.2 years.

population.label: Critically ill tracheal-intubation trial populations across ED, ICU, OR, prehospital, mixed and unspecified settings

canonical_statement: Etomidate accounted for 2,749 participants (45.5%) and ketamine for 2,600 (43.0%); all other induction nodes individually represented 2.5% or less of participants.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The most common induction agents were etomidate with 2,749 patients (45.5%) and ketamine with 2,600 patients (43.0%).

population.label: Participants randomized across induction-agent nodes

canonical_statement: Nine included studies were judged high or probably high risk of bias, while twelve were judged low or probably low risk of bias.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Nine studies were judged to be high or probably high... risk of bias and twelve were judged to be at low or probably low risk of bias.

canonical_statement: The search identified 25,577 citations, reviewed 93 full texts, and included 21 RCTs; conference abstract searching identified three additional eligible trials not yet indexed in the searched databases.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We identified 25,577 citations in the search, reviewed 93 full-texts and included 21 RCTs... Conference abstract searching identified three additional eligible trials...

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that etomidate increases adrenal suppression compared with ketamine and ketamine-propofol; both comparisons were rated high certainty.
